mappings.note: one ground point, two aeroplanes on the same vertical at 60 and 45; the answer is the DIFFERENCE of two heights over a shared base, the two-triangle pattern

string (hypotenuse) given and the height required, with tan theta supplied as a non-standard fraction so sin must be constructed from it. Single triangle, no elevation value - so C-6.1-LO-3, not C-6.3-LO-3. NOTE the stem prints tan theta = 45/8 while the solution uses 15/8 and only 15/8 gives the 8-15-17 triple
flagstaff on a tower seen from one point at 60 (top) and 45 (bottom): two nested triangles on one base, solved by eliminating the common distance
literally two observers, on OPPOSITE sides of the building, and the answer is the SUM of the two computed distances rather than a difference - the clearest two-observer item in the chapter

man on a 10 m deck sights the hill top (elevation 60) and its base (depression 30): two triangles, and the horizontal through the eye must be drawn with the 10 m deck height carried into the lower triangle
two ships on opposite sides, the 100 m gap split as x and 100 - x; the unknown height is found by eliminating x between the two triangles

only ONE angle here despite the two poles: the horizontal TR must be drawn so the working triangle has base 15 m, and the second pole's height is then 24 plus the computed rise. Single-triangle height problem, so LO-3 not LO-4
the textbook two-positions case: the SAME observer walks 20 m nearer and the elevation goes 30 to 60. LO-4's wording fits this item exactly

two shadow lengths of one tower at two sun positions, and the unknown is the ANGLE rather than a length - so the two-triangle code plus the ratio-selection code. Nothing is measured; the 3x relation does all the work
statue on a pedestal at 60 and 45 from one point; same nested-triangle structure as sha a021ef3c9389a84e with the statue in place of the flagstaff
two points at 4 m and 16 m with complementary elevations give h = root(4 x 16) = 8; numeric version of sha 113c6a95a7c24b28. The complementary relation it leans on has no legal code in this chapter
the same tower sighted from the TOP and from the BOTTOM of a 15 m building - two positions of one observer, vertically separated - so the tower height and the gap come out together

depressions of both ends of an 8 m building from one roof: two triangles, and the horizontal through the shorter building's top must be drawn to make h - 8 the working side. Same shape as sha e11633e93f2a9ebe with 8 m instead of 50 m

two positions of the PLANE (60 then 30) at constant height from one observer; the horizontal distance flown is the difference of two bases and speed follows. Two-triangle family, object moving rather than observer

observer steps 30 m back from the bank and the elevation falls 60 to 30; two positions of one observer, with the river width as the near base. Structurally identical to sha e9c81969e0edb38d in the other direction
6 m flagstaff on a tower at 45 (top) and 30 (bottom); nested triangles again, and only the tower height is asked
20 m building with a tower on top, elevations 45 and 60 from one ground point; the 5-mark long-answer duplicate of MCQ sha b710a8b028396b18
elevation 60 to the tower top and depression 45 to its foot from a 7 m roof, with the horizontal AE drawn to split the tower; the 5-mark duplicate of MCQ sha 2f65c8ccc0a66ca6

two equal poles across an 80 m road with P between them; one angle is given as a DEPRESSION from the far pole's top, which must be converted to an elevation from P before the two triangles can be combined

same 80 m road and equal poles as sha 4d01220c00efc270 but both angles stated as elevations; a near-duplicate that honestly shares the outcome, the only difference being the depression-to-elevation step

the densest item in the chapter: two named observers on opposite sides (LO-4), Deepak's 50 m roof forcing a horizontal construction and a height subtraction (C-6.2-LO-3), and the bird's height taken from a SLANT 200 m by sin 30 rather than tan (C-6.1-LO-3)
two ships on the SAME side, so the answer is the difference of the two bases; the deliberate contrast with sha 98f6c771f378e3e7 where opposite sides make it a sum
two cars on OPPOSITE sides of a 100 m tower, so the distance between them adds the two bases; paired with sha c326781cc6452886, same numbers, opposite geometry
two positions of one observer stacked VERTICALLY (Y is 40 m above X), so the horizontal YC must be drawn and the tower splits as x + 40; the vertical variant of the walk-towards-the-tower family
5 m flagstaff at 60 (top) and 30 (bottom) from one point, with BOTH the tower height and the distance asked; third member of the flagstaff family with shas a021ef3c9389a84e and c6b9b9a56a47dcec
